questions: Does the oval finish rate hold at or above the baseline's 20/20 with mean time near 1.65 s when the sensors sit at y=0.03 m?
On the s-bend and slalom, at what progress and track position does the first line loss occur, and do the outer sensors read near 1 or near 0 at that step?
Does steering oscillation fall relative to the baseline's 0.15 on the oval, which would suggest the shorter lead reduces late correction?

intent: Test the sensor lead in the opposite direction to iteration 3. Relative to the iteration-0 baseline, move all five sensors from y=0.05 m back to y=0.03 m and change nothing else. Expected result: the oval stays a near-complete finish with equal or lower steering oscillation than the baseline, and the s-bend and slalom progress rises above 0.17 and 0.12. If the oval drops below the baseline finish rate, shorter lead is also wrong and the next lever is sensor spread or footprint size.
learning: Iterations 1 to 3 suggest that the wide array with a lighter drivetrain hurts the oval, and that moving sensors forward to y=0.07 m destroyed the oval finish. The baseline lead at y=0.05 m is the best point so far. This iteration brackets the lead lever from the other side. If shorter lead also hurts, the lead optimum is near the baseline and the bend limit is likely sensor footprint or spread, to be tested next.
rationale: Race evidence so far. Iteration 0 (baseline, sensors at y=0.05 m, +/-0.024 m, 12 mm pitch, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius) is the best design at 356.6: it finishes the oval 20/20 in about 1.65 s, but goes off track on the s-bend (progress 0.17) and slalom (progress 0.12). Iteration 1 changed the array width, track, mass and wheel radius together and the oval regressed (17/20). Iteration 2 isolated the wide array with the baseline drivetrain and the oval still regressed (15/20, oscillation 0.21), so the wide array or the 0.5 kg mass hurts the oval, and the array gave only a small bend gain. Iteration 3 moved the sensors forward to y=0.07 m with the baseline drivetrain and array: the oval collapsed to 0/20 off-track (progress 0.16) and the bends barely moved (s-bend 0.21, slalom 0.12). Forward look-ahead is therefore the wrong direction; it hurts the one track that finished. The clearest signal is that a longer lead destabilises the controller-plus-geometry loop, so the opposite direction is the next test. I will keep the iteration-0 baseline exactly (array spread, 12 mm footprint, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius) and move the sensors back to y=0.03 m, a 2 cm shorter lead than baseline. This is a single-variable test. I expect the oval to stay at or above the baseline finish rate, with lower steering oscillation, and some progress gain on the s-bend and slalom if the earlier loss came from late correction. Uncertainty is high: the bend failures may be set by spread or sensor size, not lead, and I cannot yet confirm which.
